difficulty_why: Slack allows instant multi-tenant OAuth installation via unlisted Public Distribution without review, but commercial distribution requires Slack Marketplace listing review which takes up to 10 weeks and enforces strict rate limits on unlisted apps.

dev_time.label: 15-30 min
dev_time.text: Time to create a Slack app in the developer portal, configure redirect URLs, add OAuth scopes, and retrieve Client ID and Secret for local testing.

launch_time.label: Same day to 10 weeks
launch_time.text: Unlisted apps can be installed immediately by external workspaces once Public Distribution is activated (same day). If commercial distribution requires Slack Marketplace listing, review takes up to 10 business days for preliminary checks plus up to 10 weeks for functional review.

own_app_reasons.label: Custom branding
own_app_reasons.text: Display your own application name, icon, and company branding on the Slack OAuth authorization consent screen.

own_app_reasons.label: Custom OAuth scopes
own_app_reasons.text: Configure specific granular bot or user token scopes tailored to your application's unique features.

own_app_reasons.label: Dedicated API rate limits
own_app_reasons.text: Avoid sharing workspace and method rate limits with other integrations using shared multi-tenant credentials.

app_type.label: Slack App with Public Distribution
app_type.text: A Slack App created from scratch with Public Distribution enabled. Enabling Public Distribution allows multi-tenant OAuth 2.0 authorization across external customer workspaces, either as an unlisted app or listed in the Slack Marketplace.

prerequisites.label: Slack user account
prerequisites.text: A standard Slack workspace user account; no separate developer portal account or fee is required.

prerequisites.label: Slack development workspace
prerequisites.text: A Slack workspace where you have permission to install and test applications.

prerequisites.label: Workspace admin permissions
prerequisites.text: Administrative rights or admin approval in your development workspace to install apps and test OAuth token generation.

prerequisites.label: HTTPS redirect URI
prerequisites.text: A secure HTTPS redirect endpoint (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) that supports SSL.

steps.label: Create Slack App
steps.text: Navigate to the Slack App Management portal, click "Create New App", select "From scratch", enter an App Name, and select your development workspace.

fields.label: Pick a workspace to develop your app in

steps.label: Configure Redirect URLs
steps.text: In the left sidebar under Features, click "OAuth & Permissions". Scroll down to "Redirect URLs", click "Add New Redirect URL", enter the Composio redirect URI, and click "Save URLs".

steps.label: Add OAuth Scopes
steps.text: On the "OAuth & Permissions" page, scroll to "Scopes". Under "Bot Token Scopes" or "User Token Scopes", click "Add an OAuth Scope" to add the permissions needed for your integration.

fields.label: OAuth Scopes
fields.value: Add required Bot Token Scopes and User Token Scopes

steps.label: Activate Public Distribution
steps.text: In the left sidebar under Settings, click "Manage Distribution". Complete all prerequisite checklist items under "Share Your App with Other Workspaces", then click "Activate Public Distribution".

steps.label: Copy App Credentials
steps.text: In the left sidebar under Settings, click "Basic Information". Scroll to "App Credentials" and copy your Client ID and Client Secret to configure your integration in Composio.

approval.label: When required
approval.text: Marketplace app review is not required to distribute an app across workspaces via OAuth2 install links; developers can share an unlisted app with other workspaces by toggling Activate Public Distribution under Manage Distribution.

approval.label: When required
approval.text: Under the Slack API Terms of Service, Slack Marketplace review and listing is required for commercially distributed apps, whereas unlisted distribution is intended only for development, testing, and early customer pilots.

approval.label: What's checked
approval.text: Slack Marketplace review includes preliminary checks of listing documentation, scopes, and test credentials, followed by a manual functional review assessing OAuth installation, full user flow, security, and scope necessity.

approval.label: Wait
approval.text: Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days, and the functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new app submissions (or 6 weeks for updates to published apps).

approval.label: Cost
approval.text: Slack does not charge any fee for Slack Marketplace submission or listing.

approval.label: Before approval
approval.text: Before submitting for Marketplace review, apps must be installed on at least 10 active workspaces (active in the past 28 days) and have at least 10 weekly active users.

pitfalls.label: Rate limit cliff for unlisted commercial apps
pitfalls.text: Unlisted commercially distributed apps face severe API throttling on conversations.history and conversations.replies (1 req/min and max 15 objects), breaking message ingestion unless listed in the Marketplace.

pitfalls.label: Restricted search:read scope blocks Marketplace approval
pitfalls.text: The search:read scope is classified as a legacy and restricted permission; including it will cause Marketplace listing rejection, requiring migration to granular search scopes.

pitfalls.label: 10 active workspace prerequisite blocks early listing
pitfalls.text: Apps cannot submit to the Slack Marketplace without first acquiring 10 active workspaces over the last 28 days and 10 weekly active users via unlisted distribution.

pitfalls.label: Redirect URI mismatch
pitfalls.text: If multiple Redirect URLs are configured, the exact redirect_uri parameter must be sent in both the authorize and access token requests, otherwise Slack returns a bad_redirect_uri error.

pitfalls.label: Reinstallation required after scope changes
pitfalls.text: Modifying scopes does not update existing access tokens; connected workspaces must reinstall or re-authorize the app for scope additions or removals to take effect.

pitfalls.label: Configuration lock on published apps
pitfalls.text: Once listed in the Marketplace, the live app configuration is locked; modifying scopes or redirect URIs requires re-review (up to 6 weeks) and can break user installation if unapproved scopes are requested.

email_subject: Slack OAuth App Distribution and Marketplace Review Inquiry - [App Name]
email_body:
Hi Slack Platform Support Team,

I am developing an AI agent product that integrates with Slack via OAuth 2.0 to help our users automate workflows and manage conversations. Our integration connects to user workspaces using Composio.

Here are our integration details:
- App Name: [App Name]
- App ID: [Your App ID]
- Redirect URI: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add
- Scopes requested: chat:write, channels:read, channels:history, files:read, users:read, search:read.public, search:read.private, etc.

We would like to clarify a few points regarding distribution:
1. We are currently using Public Distribution as an unlisted app for onboarding our initial pilot customers. Could you confirm any specific constraints or rate limits applied to unlisted apps prior to Marketplace listing?
2. We plan to submit the app to the Slack Marketplace once we reach the 10 active workspaces threshold. Are there any specific recommendations or scope justification requirements for conversational and search scopes?
3. What is the current turnaround time for preliminary review and functional review?

Thank you for your guidance,
[Your Name]
[Your Company / Product]
[Your Contact Information]
